questions.question: Why does the project store money as branded integer paise instead of rupees as plain numbers?
options: Integers avoid floating-point rounding errors, and the brand stops plain numbers being passed as money
Brands make the values faster at runtime
questions.explanation: Integer paise keep arithmetic exact; the Paise brand adds nominal-style safety on top of structural typing.

questions.question: With `type BodyArgs<E> = E extends { body: infer B extends z.ZodType } ? [body: z.input<B>] : []`, what happens on `api("listExpenses", {})`?
options: It compiles and sends an empty body
It compiles but fails validation at runtime
It is a type error: Expected 1 arguments, but got 2
It is a type error only with noUncheckedIndexedAccess
questions.explanation: listExpenses has no body, so BodyArgs is the empty tuple and the rest parameter accepts no extra argument.

questions.question: What does the `default: return assertNever(e);` branch in `monthlyCost` give you?
options: A compile error if a new expense kind is added but not handled
Runtime validation of the expense amount
questions.explanation: After all kinds are handled, `e` is `never`. A new union member makes `e` non-never there, so the call no longer type-checks.

questions.question: When the fake server returns a record whose `amount` is the string "150.00", what does `api("listExpenses")` return?
options: A list where that amount is coerced to 15000
A list containing the bad record unchanged
`{ ok: false, error: { kind: "validation", issues: [...] } }` naming the path of the bad field
questions.explanation: The client uses safeParse at the boundary and turns failures into a typed Result, so bad data never reaches business logic.
